kept.heading: BUILDING BETTER PUBLIC SIGNALS FOR AI IMPACTS (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Analysis of 137,000 r/ChatGPT posts shows how users' experiences and expectations changed as ChatGPT became part of everyday life. Posts about therapy and companionship increased after the release of GPT-4o in May 2024 and reached about 10% of subreddit posts, while discussion of prompting declined as users became more familiar with AI. The researchers' real-time monitoring system could have detected the rise in emotional engagement by October 2024, months before broader discussion of sycophancy and AI psychosis. The findings suggest that Reddit can reveal emerging patterns in AI use and potential societal impacts that may not appear in traditional usage data.

kept.heading: BIG TECH IS CUTEWASHING ITS AI AGENTS (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Cuteness triggers the brain's pleasure centers before conscious thought, which makes people want to keep cute things close and more willing to forgive their mistakes. That makes big-eyed mascots a useful wrapper for AI agents that still hallucinate and need mass adoption. The same move made the early internet feel less intimidating in the late 1990s, then faded once the technology became routine. However, a look shared by every major AI company stops identifying any one of them and can become shorthand for what people distrust about the industry.

kept.heading: THE REASON TO BE ON REDDIT ISN'T FOR AEO (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reddit is more valuable as a mid-funnel research channel than an AEO play because developers use it to compare tools and real-world experiences before buying. Treat it like earned media by joining existing conversations without pitching. Build credibility for about 3 months before approaching moderators about AMAs or sponsored events. Focus posts on problems and lessons rather than products. Brand accounts can work when they consistently teach. Measure impact through customer interviews since Reddit influence rarely appears in analytics.

kept.heading: 5 THINGS CONTENT MARKETERS & SEOS SHOULD STOP DOING IN 2026 (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Zero-click search has made five common content habits counterproductive. Building pages around keywords misses how people now query, since the average ChatGPT prompt runs 23 words. Grading content on traffic ignores that the top-ranked page loses 58% of its CTR under an AI Overview. Publishing more matters less than maintaining what exists, as 75% of AI-cited pages were updated in the past year. The last two are relying on owned channels, when 85% of AI brand mentions come from third parties, and publishing generic guides with no original data.

kept.heading: LIFECYCLE LIVE WORKSHOP: MAPPING THE CUSTOMER JOURNEY (VIRTUAL EVENT)
kept.blurb: Phi Pham and Carlos Govantes will break down a real customer journey to identify friction and gaps across channels. You'll then map part of your own journey, such as signup to purchase or trial to paid. The workshop provides frameworks, prompts, tools, and live feedback to identify what to improve next.

kept.heading: GOOGLE SEARCH DATA ON CRAWLING, INDEXING & SERVING TIMELINES (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google shared new internal data on how long crawling, indexing, and serving processes typically take. New URLs take about 20 hours to be discovered while known URLs take about 30 days to refresh. End-to-end indexing takes about 1.5 hours when processes run normally but can stretch to months or never. Title and snippet updates typically take 1-2 days, while site moves take 1-3 months. Core update recovery can take 3-6 months. Delays can stack because each process depends on the ones before it.

kept.heading: HOW WE CATCH MESSAGING CAMPAIGN DRIFT BEFORE IT SPREADS (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Campaign drift happens when the messages a business sends shift away from what was approved. This system for SMS and RCS converts each message into an embedding and matches it against clusters of previously judged traffic. Unmatched messages are grouped into new clusters, and an LLM issues one verdict per cluster against the approved campaign details rather than per message. Human reviewers confirm or override each flag before a sender is notified, restricted, or blocked.

kept.heading: HOW WRONG IS YOUR MARKETING MIX MODEL (MMM)? (21 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: MMM becomes more reliable when media budgets are deliberately phased, so channels move independently and spend reaches different levels. Build variation into the media plan by using tactics like weekly budget changes, dark periods, and peak spend periods instead of relying on model changes to solve weak data. In the simulation, the combined approach cut variance by 70% and bias by 47% while keeping each channel's annual budget unchanged. The tradeoff was a 3.42% loss in channel-driven revenue, so use lighter phasing when that cost is too high.

kept.heading: DESKTOP HABITS HIDE MOBILE FRICTION (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Common sources of mobile friction that are missed by operators who only access the site on desktop.

kept.heading: AMAZON'S “ABOUT YOU” FEATURE DRAWS ATTENTION OVER DETAILED CUSTOMER INFERENCES (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Check Amazon's “About You” profile to see what the company has inferred about you.

kept.heading: AUDIOBOOKS ON SPOTIFY ARE GOING GLOBAL (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Spotify is expanding audiobook access from 22 to 180+ markets by the end of 2026.

kept.heading: WE CHECKED 56 OF AMERICA'S BIGGEST BRANDS: NEWSROOMS LOCK AI OUT, EVERYONE ELSE LEAVES THE DOOR OPEN (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 68% of major US brands have no AI-specific crawling rules. Newsrooms are more likely to block AI bots, with 75% restricting at least one compared with 6% of other brands. None of the 52 accessible robots.txt files fully blocked OpenAI's or Anthropic's AI search bots by name, though some blocked training crawlers. Forbes blocks training bots while allowing AI search, while GEICO explicitly allows all 12 AI crawlers it names.

kept.heading: 2026 DELOITTE HALLOWEEN SURVEY: A TREAT OF A TRADITION (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 92% of US households plan to celebrate Halloween in 2026, with average spending expected to reach $285 per household. 56% of retail shoppers plan to start shopping by September, while early shoppers expect to spend 1.7X more than others. Price and value drive purchase decisions, and 32% of Halloween shoppers expect to use generative AI for product recommendations and comparisons.

kept.heading: HOW WE INCREASED ORDERS BY 9% WITHOUT A DISCOUNT CODE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A South American gift company increased orders by 9% by adding 2 free services to its checkout summary without offering a discount. Research showed customers hesitated at the final price and wanted better value. The test highlighted existing benefits, including premium gift wrapping and a satisfaction guarantee, with both listed as free beside the total. This reframed the purchase around what customers received rather than just what they paid.

kept.heading: CHURN HAPPENS EARLY (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: SaaS churn is heavily front-loaded, with the biggest drop-off often happening during signup and initial product use before retention stabilizes. Track retention by signup cohort rather than total user churn to identify where new users leave and prioritize fixes with the greatest downstream impact. In one example, reducing signup-to-first-project churn could generate 164 additional paywall views compared with 59 from fixing the paywall step itself. Improve early experiences by helping users reach value milestones quickly, since every user lost early reduces the pool available for later conversions and referrals.

kept.heading: A NEW VISION FOR SPONSORSHIPS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Substack is expanding its sponsorship program with 3 formats that let brands fund free paid subscriptions, unlock paywalled posts, or curate themed collections from established writers. These partnerships help publishers reach new readers while generating revenue and creating opportunities to convert free readers into paying subscribers. Substack is also partnering with Kantar to measure campaign impact on brand awareness and consideration beyond impressions and clicks.

kept.heading: CLAUDE CITATIONS: CLAUDE CITES THE PAGE THAT LOOKS LIKE THE QUESTION (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Claude's citations closely match query format. Best-X questions pulled listicles 90% of the time. A-vs-B questions pulled comparison pages 87% of the time, while how-to questions pulled guides 85% of the time. Create content for each buyer query type and publish competitor comparison pages to avoid losing visibility to competitors. Sonnet and Haiku often cited different URLs for the same questions, so check both models to assess Claude visibility.

kept.heading: NOT SURE WHAT TO LAUNCH NEXT? START TALKING TO YOUR CUSTOMERS (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Study how customers use existing products to uncover winning product ideas rather than chasing trends or competitor launches. Zouk created its bestselling office bag after noticing working women needed one bag for laptops and personal items. Observe customers in real-world settings and identify workarounds that reveal unmet needs. Turn recurring complaints into product briefs and call customers to understand their frustrations. Solve functional problems first, then layer in design and cultural relevance.

kept.heading: BEFORE YOU REBRAND: HOW A BRAND AUDIT REVEALS WHAT ACTUALLY NEEDS TO CHANGE (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Conduct a brand audit before rebranding to identify the real problem. Compare internal strategy with customer feedback to determine whether the issue requires clearer messaging or a new identity. Review public touchpoints to find gaps between the intended brand and customer perception. Match each finding to the right fix rather than defaulting to a full redesign. Preserve existing brand equity and ensure the customer experience supports the brand promise.

kept.heading: IS THIS A JOB FOR A HUMAN OR AI? (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Use the HUMAN framework to decide which tasks belong to AI versus people.

kept.blurb: 12 tips for generating B2B leads through buyer-focused content, tailored lead magnets, and email nurturing.
